An invalid token is a\n    // successful OPERATION (it ran to completion); only a thrown error is 'error'.\n    const stop = this.authMetrics?.startOperation('token_validation');\n    try {\n      const result = await this.authService.validateToken(token);\n      if (!result.valid || !result.payload) {\n        stop?.('success');\n        return { valid: false };\n      }\n\n      // Calculate expiration from JWT exp claim or default to 15 minutes from now\n      const expiresAt = result.payload.exp\n        ? new Date(result.payload.exp * 1000)\n        : new Date(Date.now() + 15 * 60 * 1000);\n\n      stop?.('success');\n      return {\n        valid: true,\n        userId: result.payload.sub,\n        tenantId: result.payload.tenantId ?? undefined,\n        role: result.payload.role,\n        expiresAt,\n      };\n    } catch (err) {\n      stop?.('error');\n      throw err;\n    }\n  }\n}\n","numLines":43,"startLine":296,"totalLines":338}}}

Both were removed. These tests make re-introduction loud:\n20\t * adding the method back fails CI until a deliberate architectural decision\n21\t * (a \"new tenant + first admin\" onboarding saga) replaces it.\n22\t */\n23\tdescribe('Public surface contract (SEC-CRITICAL-001 / MT-LOW-001)', () => {\n24\t  it('AuthResolver does NOT expose a register mutation', () => {\n25\t    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthResolver.prototype, 'register');\n26\t    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n27\t  });\n28\t\n29\t  it('AuthenticationService does NOT expose a register method', async () => {\n30\t    const { AuthenticationService } = await import('../services/authentication.service');\n31\t    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthenticationService.prototype, 'register');\n32\t    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n33\t  });\n34\t\n35\t  it('tenantBySlug implementation returns only name/slug/logoUrl keys', async () => {\n36\t    // The leaky row the resolver must NOT forward: a full tenant entity whose\n37\t    // `id`/`status`/`plan` are exactly the fields MT-LOW-001 removed from the\n38\t    // public payload. `stub<Tenant>` keeps those field names checked against\n39\t    // the real entity, so a rename cannot quietly turn this into a fixture\n40\t    // that proves nothing.\n41\t    const leakyTenant = stub<Tenant>({\n42\t      id: 'internal-uuid-must-not-leak',\n43\t      name: 'Acme Farms',\n44\t      slug: 'acme',\n45\t      logoUrl: null,\n46\t      status: TenantStatus.ACTIVE,\n47\t      plan: TenantPlan.ENTERPRISE,\n48\t    });\n49\t    const resolver = new TenantResolver(\n50\t      collaborator<TenantService>(\n51\t        { findBySlug: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(leakyTenant)) },\n52\t        'TenantService',\n53\t      ),\n54\t      // The audit and command collaborators are unreachable from the public\n55\t      // query; an empty `collaborator` makes any future call to them a named\n56\t      // failure instead of a silent `undefined is not a function`.\n57\t      collaborator<AuditLogService>({}, 'AuditLogService'),\n58\t      collaborator<TenantProvisioningCommandService>({}, 'TenantProvisioningCommandService'),\n59\t    );\n60\t\n61\t    const result = await resolver.tenantBySlug('acme');\n62\t\n63\t    // WHY exact-keys assertion: a future field addition to the public payload\n64\t    // must be a deliberate decision, not an accidental spread. The exact key\n65\t    // set also structurally proves `id` and `status` are absent.\n66\t    expect(Object.keys(result).sort()).toEqual(['logoUrl', 'name', 'slug']);\n67\t  });\n68\t});\n69\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"b0986a18-d50a-4b67-8030-53f09c521777","uuid":"1987fa5a-c4d5-4acb-9f7e-6e06469e49ee","timestamp":"2026-10-05T10:14:52.223Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/gharunner/actions-runner/_work/aquaculture_platform/aquaculture_platform/aria-worktrees/req-AIR-aria-evidence-judge-e54fc625b415/apps/auth-service/src/modules/authentication/__tests__/public-surface-contract.spec.ts","content":"import 'reflect-metadata';\n\nimport { collaborator, stub } from '@aquaculture/testing';\n\nimport { AuditLogService } from '../../../audit/audit-log.service';\nimport { Tenant, TenantPlan, TenantStatus } from '../../tenant/entities/tenant.entity';\nimport { TenantResolver } from '../../tenant/resolvers/tenant.resolver';\nimport { TenantProvisioningCommandService } from '../../tenant/services/tenant-provisioning-command.service';\nimport { TenantService } from '../../tenant/services/tenant.service';\nimport { AuthResolver } from '../resolvers/auth.resolver';\n\n/**\n * Public-surface contract — SEC-CRITICAL-001 + MT-LOW-001 regression guards.\n *\n * WHY: the 2026-06-10 audit found the public `register` mutation accepted a\n * client-supplied tenantId with zero validation (anonymous cross-tenant\n * account injection), and the public `tenantBySlug` query leaked the internal\n * tenant UUID + lifecycle status — the exact harvest leg feeding the\n * injection. Both were removed. These tests make re-introduction loud:\n * adding the method back fails CI until a deliberate architectural decision\n * (a \"new tenant + first admin\" onboarding saga) replaces it.\n */\ndescribe('Public surface contract (SEC-CRITICAL-001 / MT-LOW-001)', () => {\n  it('AuthResolver does NOT expose a register mutation', () => {\n    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthResolver.prototype, 'register');\n    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n\n  it('AuthenticationService does NOT expose a register method', async () => {\n    const { AuthenticationService } = await import('../services/authentication.service');\n    const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(AuthenticationService.prototype, 'register');\n    expect(descriptor).toBeUndefined();\n  });\n\n  it('tenantBySlug implementation returns only name/slug/logoUrl keys', async () => {\n    // The leaky row the resolver must NOT forward: a full tenant entity whose\n    // `id`/`status`/`plan` are exactly the fields MT-LOW-001 removed from the\n    // public payload. `stub<Tenant>` keeps those field names checked against\n    // the real entity, so a rename cannot quietly turn this into a fixture\n    // that proves nothing.\n    const leakyTenant = stub<Tenant>({\n      id: 'internal-uuid-must-not-leak',\n      name: 'Acme Farms',\n      slug: 'acme',\n      logoUrl: null,\n      status: TenantStatus.ACTIVE,\n      plan: TenantPlan.ENTERPRISE,\n    });\n    const resolver = new TenantResolver(\n      collaborator<TenantService>(\n        { findBySlug: jest.fn(() => Promise.resolve(leakyTenant)) },\n        'TenantService',\n      ),\n      // The audit and command collaborators are unreachable from the public\n      // query;
